articles.title: Rams star Myles Garrett could reportedly be sidelined longer than expected
articles.summary: Garrett could potentially be out until nearly the midway point of the season.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams star pass rusher Myles Garrett could remain sidelined from knee surgery until nearly the halfway point of the season, NFL Network reported .

Garrett was given a six-week timeline after his knee surgery, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported. That could potentially keep him out until the Rams' Week 9 game against the Washington Commanders on Nov. 8.

Garrett is "determined to beat the timeline," but the Rams want to be cautious with his recovery, Rapoport reported. Garrett has a minimum four-game stint on the IR, which means the earliest he could return is Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18.

Garrett underwent arthroscopic surgery on his left knee after struggling in Los Angeles ' Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . The knee had bothered him throughout training camp and the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year didn't record a single tackle against the 49ers.

The Rams acquired Garrett in a blockbuster offseason trade with the Cleveland Browns that sent Jared Verse and multiple draft picks to Cleveland.

Rams coach Sean McVay has not publicly announced a specific timeline for Garrett's return.

articles.title: Cowboys and Lions among teams to call Steelers about potential trade for Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: Porter has yet to play this season as he recovers from a back injury and seeks a new contract.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions have inquired about Joey Porter Jr. as a potential trade market for the Pittsburgh Steelers star cornerback begins to take shape, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported.

The Cowboys and Lions were among "a handful of teams" who have called the Steelers about Porter, ESPN reported. The Steelers are said to be willing to listen to offers.

The Cowboys and Lions have both suffered significant injuries to their secondary since the start of the season.

Porter has yet to play this season as he recovers from a back injury and is listed as questionable for Pittsburgh's Week 3 game against the Cincinnati Bengals .

He also is seeking a new contract but said this week that he will play this season once he is healthy . Pittsburgh historically has not engaged in contract renegotiations during the season.

Porter spoke for the first time this week since the start of the season and called the passing of his contract extension deadline "old news."

Porter also addressed reports that he sought a second opinion on his injury, calling them false. And he denied asking the Steelers for a trade despite reports suggesting that was the case .

articles.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams reportedly has Grade 2 hamstring injury and could be sidelined for a month
articles.summary: Williams injured his hamstring near the end of the Bears' loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring injury and could potentially be out up to a month, ESPN reported .

Williams injured his hamstring near the end of the Bears' loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.

The estimated timeline for a Grade 2 hamstring injury is three-to-four weeks, though Williams is determined to be back sooner, ESPN reported.

The Bears have called Williams only "week-to-week." He is out for their Week 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles . Backup QB Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol and has not yet been cleared to play. Case Keenum could start against the Eagles in their place.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson initially told reporters that the news on Williams' injury was "somewhat encouraging." He also acknowledged that Williams is "likely to miss some time."

ESPN reported that the Bears "have tried to keep the extent of his injury under wraps for competitive-purpose advantages."

"This guy's a little bit different than the average human being," Johnson told reporters earlier this week. "I said that last night, I'll double down on that. He gets back — he has in the past — a lot faster than what people can anticipate, and so I'm not putting a timeline on this. We're going to say week-to-week. He's going to attack this with everything that he knows."

articles.title: Puka Nacua injury update: Rams star could return in Week 4, surgery still on the table if he can't improve
articles.summary: The Rams believe Puka Nacua is dealing with a short-term injury.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams star wideout Puka Nacua is unlikely to play when the team takes the field for Week 3's game against the Denver Broncos on Sunday night. While he hasn't been ruled out yet, Nacua was listed as doubtful on the team's injury report after not practicing the entire week due to a groin injury.

But the team believes it's possible Nacua will be back in Week 4, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. The team believes Nacua is capable of taking the field now, but would not show the same level of explosiveness. Because of that, the Rams view Nacua's injury as a short-term thing, and believe he'll get back to work soon.

With that said, it's still possible Nacua could undergo surgery on his groin. If the wideout doesn't show improvement, a procedure would be the next option. The team, however, does not believe Nacua needs to have surgery to correct the issue.

Nacua, 25, has been sidelined since the team's Week 1 game against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Nacua played in that contest, hauling in five catches for 74 yards, but developed groin and hip issues during the game. Despite a long layoff between Week 1 and Week 2, Nacua was unable to face the New York Giants last week.

While Nacua apparently managed both issues, Schefter reported Sunday that Nacua's groin is the main concern.

Rams head coach Sean McVay caused some concern ahead of Week 3 when he said Nacua was " not making great progress " in his return from the injury. McVay described the issue as "pre-hernia" and said the team would err on the side of caution with Nacua. "Once you get to a certain point," McVay added, "then I think you feel pretty good moving forward."

The Rams are hopeful that can happen as soon as the team's Week 4 game against the Philadelphia Eagles . The team, however, should have little incentive to rush him back. Despite missing Nacua in Week 2, the Rams pulled off a dominant 28-6 win over the Giants. It was a return to form after the Rams were easily dispatched by the 49ers in Week 1, and gave the team and Nacua some breathing room moving forward.

articles.title: Jason and Kylie Kelce’s latest $2.9 billion market move marks a new milestone as their investment reaches 5,000+ stores
articles.summary: Jason Kelce is expanding his post-NFL business portfolio, with his latest move taking him into the growing hot sauce market.
articles.body: Jason Kelce is expanding his post-NFL business portfolio, with his latest move taking him into the growing hot sauce market. Through Winnie Capital, the family office supporting the business and philanthropic activities of Jason and Kylie Kelce, a strategic equity investment has been made in Hank Sauce, the Sea Isle City, New Jersey-based brand that has grown from a local favorite into a product sold in thousands of stores. The deal gives Hank Sauce another major name behind its plans for wider national distribution while also adding a growing consumer brand to the Kelces’ business interests.Jason Kelce backs a brand he already knew wellHank Sauce announced the strategic equity investment from Winnie Capital on December 22, 2025. Neither side disclosed the financial terms, meaning the amount invested and the size of the equity stake remain private.Kelce’s connection to Hank Sauce, however, goes beyond the investment. The former Philadelphia Eagles center has spent considerable time around South Jersey over the years and was already familiar with Hank Sauce and its Sea Isle City restaurant before the business relationship developed.According to reporting surrounding the deal, Winnie Capital formally connected with the Hank Sauce founders in September 2024. That eventually developed into the investment announced more than a year later.This distinction is important. Kelce is not simply appearing in an advertising campaign for the company. Winnie Capital has taken an equity position in the existing business, while Jason is also expected to contribute to brand awareness, content and marketing as Hank Sauce attempts to reach a larger audience.Kylie Kelce is connected to the deal through Winnie Capital, which serves as the family office for the couple’s business and philanthropic activities. The announcement does not disclose a separate personal investment from Kylie, so her role is more accurately described through the family’s investment operation.Jason also brings something that cannot be measured simply by the undisclosed investment figure. After 13 NFL seasons with the Eagles and a growing media career that includes the New Heights podcast with Travis Kelce, he has an audience that can introduce Hank Sauce to consumers far beyond its Jersey Shore base.Hank Sauce has already reached more than 5,000 storesWinnie Capital is investing in a company that has already spent years building its business.Brian “Hank” Ruxton, Matt Pittaluga and Josh Jaspan founded Hank Sauce in 2011. The business started on a much smaller scale before gradually expanding its production, restaurant operation and retail distribution.Hank Sauce now says its products are available in more than 5,000 retail locations nationwide. Its distribution includes retailers such as Publix, GIANT, ACME, ShopRite, Sprouts, Cabela’s and Ace Hardware, giving the company a footprint that already stretches well beyond New Jersey.The business also operates from a 10,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Millville, New Jersey, a major change from its early years when production was considerably smaller and bottles were made by hand.Its Sea Isle City restaurant, meanwhile, dates back to 2012 and remains an important part of the company’s connection to the Jersey Shore.The product itself was built around a straightforward idea. Rather than competing only on extreme heat, Hank Sauce has focused heavily on flavor. That approach has allowed the company to appeal to customers who enjoy hot sauce without necessarily looking for the hottest product possible.Winnie Capital investment comes as Hank Sauce targets a much bigger marketHank Sauce is trying to expand in a sizeable category. The U.S. hot sauce market has been valued at roughly $2.9 billion, according to market figures cited in reporting surrounding Kelce’s investment.The opportunity for Hank Sauce is therefore much larger than its original Jersey Shore customer base.The company already has several pieces needed for further expansion, including its own production facility, more than 5,000 retail locations, an established product lineup and over a decade of operating history. The next challenge is increasing national recognition while continuing to add retailers, restaurants and other distribution channels.That is where Winnie Capital’s investment and Jason Kelce’s involvement could play a role. Along with providing capital, the partnership is expected to include work around content, marketing and brand visibility.For Kylie Kelce, the deal is connected to the broader activities of the family office she shares with Jason rather than a separately announced personal investment. For Jason, it gives him an equity interest through Winnie Capital in a company he was already familiar with as a consumer.Hank Sauce has now been operating for around 15 years, has expanded into more than 5,000 stores and produces its sauces from a 10,000-square-foot New Jersey facility. articles.title: De'Von Achane limps off field with knee injury on Dolphins' first drive
articles.summary: De'Von Achane touched the ball multiple times on the team's first drive before the injury.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins came into the season with low expectations, but running back De'Von Achane was the one player who could carry the team to respectability. But the Dolphins experienced their worst-case scenario in Week 3, as Achane limped off the field on the team's first offensive drive.

Achane's injury came on the team's fifth play of the game. He had three carries for 17 yards on the Dolphins ' first drive before the injury.

Achane was able to get up after the play, but was tended to by trainers before he gingerly exited the field.

He eventually walked back to the locker room and was deemed questionable to return with a knee injury.

Any missed time for Achane would be devastating for a Dolphins team bereft of offensive talent. After cutting Tua Tagovailoa and Tyreek Hill , and trading away Jaylen Waddle , Achane was the last man standing on offense.

While Miami could have traded Achane away, the team instead opted to give the 24-year-old a four-year, $68 million extension. He was expected to be the focal point of the team's new-look offense with Malik Willis under center.

Since joining the NFL in 2023, Achane has emerged as a star. He turned in his best season in the NFL last year, rushing for 1,350 yards and scoring eight rushing touchdowns. That performance resulted in Achane being elected to the Pro Bowl for the first time in his career.

articles.title: Are Justin Herbert and Patrick Herbert brothers? Their Oregon and Chargers connection explained
articles.summary: Patrick Herbert is about to experience an NFL moment that has been years in the making.
articles.body: Patrick Herbert is about to experience an NFL moment that has been years in the making. The Los Angeles Chargers elevated the tight end from their practice squad Saturday ahead of their Week 3 matchup against the Buffalo Bills, putting him in line to make his NFL regular-season debut alongside his older brother, Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. For the Herbert family, however, this is not the first time the brothers have shared a football field.Justin and Patrick were previously teammates at the University of Oregon in 2019. Seven years later, they are reunited as NFL teammates, only this time with Justin throwing passes in the NFL and Patrick trying to make his mark at tight end.Meet Patrick Herbert, Justin Herbert's younger brother who is making his NFL debut Patrick Herbert is a 25-year-old tight end who played college football at Oregon, following in the footsteps of his older brother. Three years younger than Justin, Patrick spent six seasons with the Ducks from 2019 through 2024. He finished his Oregon career with 31 receptions for 388 yards and four touchdowns, including six starts during his senior season in 2024.Unlike his brother, Patrick did not enter the NFL as a highly touted first-round selection. He went undrafted in the 2025 NFL Draft and signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars as an undrafted free agent. After failing to make Jacksonville's initial 53-man roster, Herbert spent the 2025 season on the Jaguars' practice squad. That made his path to an NFL game considerably different from Justin's.Patrick Herbert followed Justin to OregonPatrick arrived at Oregon in 2019 while Justin was entering his senior season as the Ducks' starting quarterback. Justin helped lead Oregon to a 12-2 record that season and a Rose Bowl victory, while Patrick appeared in two games as a true freshman. Despite being teammates, the brothers never connected for a pass.Patrick did not record a reception during that 2019 season, meaning Justin never had the opportunity to throw his younger brother a game pass. Their reunion with the Chargers therefore creates a chance to finish something they started at Oregon but this time on an NFL field.How did Patrick Herbert end up with the Chargers?After spending the 2025 season with Jacksonville, Patrick joined the Chargers' practice squad in 2026, reuniting with Justin. The move gave the brothers another opportunity to be teammates after their brief overlap at Oregon. Reuters reported that Patrick signed with Los Angeles in September after spending the previous season with the Jaguars.Patrick's promotion to the active roster came because the Chargers were dealing with injuries at tight end. With David Njoku and Charlie Kolar unavailable, Patrick was elevated to provide additional depth for the matchup against Buffalo. CBS Sports reported that Herbert was expected to serve as the team's No. 3 tight end behind Oronde Gadsden and Hayden Rucci.Patrick Herbert and Justin Herbert could make NFL historyThe most intriguing part of Sunday's reunion is obvious: Could Justin Herbert throw a pass to Patrick Herbert? The brothers never connected at Oregon, so a completion between them would be a first for their professional careers.And a touchdown would carry even more historical significance. NBC Sports reported that the last brother-to-brother touchdown pass in an NFL game came in 1929, when Chicago Bears quarterback Red Grange threw a touchdown pass to his brother Gardie Grange. The only other known brother-to-brother touchdown pass came in 1924.That means a Justin-to-Patrick touchdown would be an extremely rare NFL occurrence. articles.title: Drake Maye fumbles on pass attempt without being touched for his league-high fifth turnover of the season
articles.summary: A turnover-plagued season for Drake Maye hit a new low on Sunday.
articles.body:
A turnover-plagued season for Drake Maye hit a new low on Sunday.

The New England Patriots were driving on their second possession in a scoreless game against the Jacksonville Jaguars . On first-and-10 from the Jacksonville 35, Maye dropped back for a pass and appeared to be targeting wide receiver Kyle Williams , who had one-on-one coverage on a post route down the right sideline.

But he forgot one thing — to throw the ball. Just before he brought his arm forward to pass, the ball slipped from Maye's hand.

Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton recovered the ball, and a promising Patriots possession was over.

Maye wasn't hit. He wasn't even under pressure. The ball just slipped from his hand. Replay confirmed the call on the field that the ball came loose before his arm moved forward.

Here's another look in slow-motion confirming that the ball was out.

Making matters worse for the Patriots, the Jaguars converted the turnover into a 10-play, 62-yard touchdown drive for a 7-0 lead.

The turnover was Maye's fifth this season and his 13th since the start of last season's playoffs in six-plus games. His five turnovers through the first quarter of Sunday's game were tied for the most in the NFL with Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush . As of the time of Sunday's first-quarter fumble, Maye had tallied just one touchdown this season.

By comparison, Maye totaled 11 turnovers in 17 games over the course of the entire 2025 regular season in route to All-Pro honors and a runner-up finish in the MVP race. Until he fixes his turnover issues, the Patriots are going to have a difficult time gaining traction in their quest to repeat as AFC champions.

articles.title: Watch as Drake Maye's turnover woes continue by letting go of ball for strange fumble vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: Maye now has a turnover in every game this season after strangely letting go of the football in Week 3.
articles.body:
Drake Maye hasn't looked anything like the 2025 version of himself so far in 2026.

After finishing as the runner-up in MVP voting last season, displaying precise passing, strong decision making and athleticism to scramble when necessary, Maye has had a lackluster opening stretch to his third NFL season.

Through two games, Maye was already tied for the league lead in interceptions. Then, on Sunday against the Jaguars , he had one of the most bizarre fumbles you'll see from a quarterback, letting go of the ball despite no pressure.

Here's a look at Maye's latest turnover and how it added to a concerning trend for the Patriots quarterback.

Drake Maye lets go of ball during pass for fumble vs. Jaguars

New England was on the road to face Jacksonville in Week 3, and after going scoreless on their opening drive, the Patriots got the ball back around the mid-way point of the first quarter.

After Rhamondre Stevenson picked up a first down, however, Maye had a strange fumble on the following play. He wasn't being pressured by any Jaguars defenders, and after faking a handoff and looking to throw deep, Maye simply let go of the ball while winding up his pass.

The ball fell to the ground, and DaVon Hamilton jumped on it for a fumble.

There appeared to be no other excuse than the ball slipping out of Maye's hand:

Maye's fumble against the Jaguars represented his fifth turnover already this season. No NFL player has more.

According to Matt McCarthy, 17 of the Patriots opponents' 23 points this season have come off Maye turnovers.

The Patriots quarterback threw three interceptions in one quarter against the Seahawks in Week 1, a loss for New England, then threw another pick against the Steelers with no touchdown passes in Week 2.

Turnovers are quickly growing into a significant concern for the young star after leading his team to the Super Bowl last season.

articles.title: Dabhal gram sabha seeks exclusion of Mhaisal, Kamarkand from ESA list
articles.summary: Kirlapal-Dabhal gram sabha urges removal of Mhaisal and Kamarkand from Western Ghats ESA list, citing concerns over housing, roads and livelihoods.
articles.body: Margao: Villagers of Kirlapal-Dabhal have demanded that Mhaisal and Kamarkand be excluded from the proposed Western Ghats ecologically sensitive area (ESA) list, fearing the designation will restrict construction, repairs and other activities in the villages.At a special gram sabha, villagers passed a resolution seeking the exclusion of the two villages from the ESA proposal. They also resolved to forward all objections received over the past several days to the authorities the same day to meet the deadline for filing them.“Our demand is that both villages be excluded from the ESA. If the entire villages cannot be excluded, then at least the residential areas and private properties in these villages should be kept out,” a villager said.Villagers said an ESA tag could affect basic amenities and livelihoods. “If these villages are brought under the ESZ, residents will not be able to build or repair their houses, roads cannot be built in the villages, and fencing for plantations will not be allowed,” another villager said.Sarpanch Damodar Bandekar backed the villagers’ stand.The demand comes amid Union environment ministry’s fifth draft notification issued this year, which proposes 108 Goa villages, covering 1,461 sq km across Sattari, Canacona, Dharbandora and Sanguem talukas, as ecologically sensitive areas of the Western Ghats.State govt has opposed the proposed list since 2024. It initially sought the exclusion of 47 villages and later reduced its demand to 21 villages, seeking a final list of 87 ESA villages.The draft notification, issued on July 27, prohibits mining, quarrying and sand mining within ESAs. articles.title: Broncos player punished by the NFL ahead of important Rams game
articles.summary: A Denver Broncos player just got some bad news ahead of the Los Angeles Rams game.
articles.body:
It doesn't get much bigger in the NFL than a primetime game for all to see, and the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Rams have just that tonight. They play each other in Denver for a "Sunday Night Football" matchup.

Last week, the Broncos beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 20-13 game, so the Broncos are flying high on that win. Both the Broncos and Rams are 1-1 going into this game, so the stakes are high, and it's already an important early-season showdown.

But one Denver player is coming into the game after getting disciplined by the NFL. He was served with a fine on Saturday for actions taken in that game against the Jaguars.

Alex Singleton gets fined ahead of Broncos-Rams showdown

Each Saturday, the league makes decisions to discipline players for breaking the NFL's rules during the games the week prior. According to the NFL's official website , the league "uses the fine schedule to outline the league's and the union's expectations for players to conduct themselves in a way that honors the sport and respects the game, themselves, their fellow players, the fans and the league."

Over the weekend, the NFL fined Alex Singleton of the Denver Broncos $17,911 for unnecessary roughness after he was penalized for a hit on a defenseless player in Week 3. That's one of the bigger fines of the weekend, too. The NFL announced the news in the league's official accountability report .

He's allowed to challenge the punishment. But if he pays it up, the good news is that the fines collected go to the Professional Athletes Foundation and the NFL Foundation , so it's for a noble cause.

articles.title: Josh Allen throws interceptions on consecutive passes after 195 straight attempts without one
articles.summary: Genesis Smith made two excellent plays on Josh Allen in Week 3.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills star Josh Allen entered play in Week 3 on a lengthy interception-less streak. But Allen met his kryptonite Sunday, and it came in the form of Los Angeles Chargers rookie Genesis Smith.

Smith picked off Allen in the first quarter Sunday, ending Allen's 195-attempt streak without an interception. It was the longest such active streak in the NFL.

Smith read the play — of Allen's eyes — perfectly, jumping in front of the intended receiver to make the play.

The Chargers capitalized on Smith's interception, driving down the field and kicking a field goal to take a 10-0 lead over Buffalo.

That put Allen in a spot he hasn't been in all season: Trailing by double digits.

He responded to that adversity by … throwing an interception on his next pass. This one also wound up in Smith's arms.

This time around, Smith showed off his speed and ball instincts, running with Bills wideout DJ Moore all the way down the field and coming up with an incredible catch for the interception.

It was a shocking start for the Bills and Allen, who dropped 36 points in Week 1 and 41 points in Week 2. Allen played a massive role in the team's excellence, scoring nine total touchdowns in those contests.

But that was before he ran into Smith. The fourth-round rookie had not started for the Chargers during the first two weeks of the regular season. By the end of the first quarter Sunday, he was already well on his way to the finest game of his young career.

articles.title: De'Von Achane Injured, Latest on Dolphins RB After Exit vs. Chiefs & Ollie Gordon II Fantasy Outlook
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane was ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs with what could be a significant injury:
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane was ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs with what could be a significant injury:

Achane exited early in the first quarter before the Dolphins provided the update in the third.

Running back Jaylen Wright was ruled out ahead of the game due to a stinger and a foot injury.

Ollie Gordon II will be slated to lead the Dolphins' run game for the remainder of the Week 3 matchup.

Achane fell after an awkward tackle on a short run early in the Dolphins' opening offensive drive.

His last play of the game was an 11-yard run for a first down, after which he was slow to get up.

The running back is visiting the sideline medical tent before walking off the field under his own power.

Achane later returned to the Dolphins' sideline without pads but walking without a visible limp, per Melanie Collins of CBS.

Wright was limited throughout the week before he was ruled out of practice Friday with his injuries.

Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Friday he was "confident" Gordon could take on a larger role in Wright's absence.

There will now be even more pressure on Gordon to step up for Achane, who went into Sunday having recorded a team-high 31 carries while tying for the Dolphins lead with seven catches.

Gordon, 22, played just 15 offensive snaps and 13 special teams snaps over the first two games of the season, over which he amassed three carries for seven yards.

He could have increased fantasy upside if Achane, who had been on the field for more than 80 percent of the Dolphins' offensive snaps so far this season, misses extended time with his knee injury.

The Dolphins are also missing top wideout Caleb Douglas to an ankle injury. Malik Washington and Chris Bell could also see a bump in usage should the Dolphins focus on their passing game now that the team's top two running backs are sidelined.

articles.title: Drake Maye Ripped by NFL Fans for Turnovers During Brutal Start to Patriots Season
articles.summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is not having the season start he was hoping for following his 2025 MVP runner-up campaign.
articles.body:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is not having the season start he was hoping for following his 2025 MVP runner-up campaign.

Maye committed his seventh turnover in three games by throwing a third-quarter interception Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

He was later benched for Tommy DeVito with the Jaguars leading 35-6 in the fourth quarter.

After the game, Maye discussed the matter:

NFL fans were left stunned by Maye's 1-to-6 season-long touchdown to interception ratio through 11 quarters of the season.

The Patriots' first drive Sunday resulted in a punt. Maye lost the ball while attempting a pass to end the second.

Maye ran in a 21-yard touchdown that was waved off by an offensive holding penalty in the second quarter. The drive ultimately ended in a field goal.

The Patriots lost control again on their final drive of the half. After recovering his own fumble on a scramble earlier in the possession, Maye sent a red-zone interception into the arms of Jags defender Travis Hunter.

The Patriots missed a field goal on their first drive of the third quarter before Maye threw an interception on the first play of his team's next possession.

The broadcast showed Patriots coach Mike Vrabel having a talk with Maye on the sideline after his second pick of the game.

Vrabel kept Maye in for the start of the fourth quarter, at which point his team trailed 28-3, before turning DeVito to finish out the game.

Maye recorded his lone touchdown of the season so far on a short pass to Eli Raridon early in a season-opening 13-10 loss to the defending champion Seattle Seahawks.

The Patriots won 20-3 in Week 2 after holding the Pittsburgh Steelers to a single field goal as linebacker Elijah Ponder scored New England's lone touchdown of the game on a fumble recovery.

New England will hope to see their starting quarterback regain some of the confidence he showed while leading his team to a Super Bowl appearance last season in order to bounce back next Sunday at the Buffalo Bills.

articles.title: Breece Hall Injured, Latest on Jets RB After Exit vs. Lions & Braelon Allen Fantasy Outlook
articles.summary: The New York Jets ruled out running back Breece Hall for the remainder of Sunday's matchup against the Detroit Lions with a thigh injury, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The New York Jets ruled out running back Breece Hall for the remainder of Sunday's matchup against the Detroit Lions with a thigh injury, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

That leaves Braelon Allen atop the depth chart at the position, with Isaiah Davis also available.

Hall, 25, suffered the injury after being tackled and twisted out of bounds, near the end zone, during the fourth quarter. He appeared to land hard on his right leg. He had rushed 13 times for 32 yards and caught three passes for 23 yards before the injury.

He has been clearly atop the pecking order in New York's backfield this season and was putting up low-end RB1 numbers. That makes his potential loss a big one for both the Jets and fantasy players who drafted him.

It could open the door for Allen from a fantasy perspective, however, making him a must-add player on waivers this week. Coming into Sunday he had rushed for 457 yards and four touchdowns in 23 career games across parts of three seasons in what has primarily been a complementary role to Hall.

Allen is rostered in just 18 percent of Yahoo leagues, so he likely will be available. Anybody will Hall on the roster has to prioritize him on waivers, but if you are low on options at the running back or flex, he's a fantastic target.

Granted, much will depend on Hall's injury status. If he's not slated to miss any time, Allen loses any value beyond his status as a handcuff. But if Hall is looking at a longer-term stint on the sidelines, Allen is going to be the most popular addition in fantasy football this week. Consider him a very solid flex option if he's forced into starting duty.

articles.title: NFL Fans React to Chargers, Texans Falling to 0-3 After High Preseason Expectations
articles.summary: Two Super Bowl LXI hopefuls are at risk of missing the playoffs altogether after winless starts to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Two Super Bowl LXI hopefuls are at risk of missing the playoffs altogether after winless starts to the 2026 season.

The Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans both fell to 0-3 on the season following Sunday losses.

Justin Herbert threw a critical interception late in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills, while the Houston Texans were unable to stop a game-deciding field goal drive in a 19-17 loss to the Indianapolis Colts.

Some viewers were surprised to see both teams still without a victory heading into the month of October.

The Chargers gained a 10-0 lead in the first quarter before going into the half with Sunday's game tied at 10 points apiece.

The Bills ultimately won despite turning over the ball five times, a feat ESPN Insights reported the team hadn't accomplished since 1997, after the Chargers scored just 10 points off turnovers.

This marks the first time since 2017 the Chargers have started out a season 0-3. Los Angeles went on to go 9-7 and miss the playoffs that season.

The Texans have more recent experience with a slow start. Houston started out 0-3 last season before going 12-2 down the stretch to make it into the playoffs.

ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime pointed out two of the Texans'. three season-opening losses last year took place against NFC teams.

All three Texans losses so far this fall have been against AFC opponents, which could have a greater impact on postseason tiebreakers.

The Texans will need more consistent production from an offense that went three-and-out twice while trailing in Sunday's third quarter in order to replicate last season's comeback.

The 2025 Texans were one of seven teams to ever make it to the NFL postseason following an 0-3 start, per Josh Dubow of the Associated Press.

The Chargers and Texans will now be tasked with beating the odds by turning things around starting in Week 4. The Texans face the visiting Dallas Cowboys next Sunday, the same day the Chargers travel to play the defending champion Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel Says His Concern Level Is 'Very High' After Maye, Patriots' Blowout Loss to Jaguars
articles.summary: Mike Vrabel is not pleased with the New England Patriots three games into the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Mike Vrabel is not pleased with the New England Patriots three games into the 2026 season.

"My concern level is very high for this football team," he told reporters following Sunday's 35-6 loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars, dropping the Pats to 1-2.

Quarterback Drake Maye—last year's MVP runner-up—had a brutal game against Jacksonville, throwing two interceptions, taking three sacks and losing a fumble. His three turnovers directly led to 14 points, a total that could have been 17, though Cam Little missed an audacious 70-yard field goal attempt to end the first half.

Live Live: Updates from every NFL Week 3 game

Maye now has seven turnovers on the season and called Sunday's performance "unacceptable."

One of the critiques regarding the Patriots during last year's Super Bowl run was that they benefitted from the NFL's easiest schedule (and one of the easiest schedules in NFL history ). Then in the playoffs they faced a Los Angeles Chargers team with a decimated offensive line, a Houston Texans team without Nico Collins (Dalton Schultz also left the game injured in the first half) and a Denver Broncos team without Bo Nix.

The Seattle Seahawks were healthy in the Super Bowl, however, and smoked New England 29-13, a game that was far more lopsided than even the 16-point deficit suggests.

And with losses against the Seahawks and Jaguars to start the 2026 season—both playoff teams from a year ago and legitimate Super Bowl contenders this year—a narrative is emerging. Perhaps last year's Super Bowl run was a bit luckier than folks in New England want to admit.

The 2026 season is young, of course, and Maye and the Patriots have plenty of time to turn things around. Doing so in the short term won't be easy, however, with the undefeated Buffalo Bills up next.

articles.title: Steelers Beat Bengals, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Rodgers, Burrow, Chase, Higgins, Top Players
articles.summary: Sunday was a quarterback showdown.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers came out on top against the Cincinnati Bengals and Joe Burrow, handing them their first loss of the season with a 30-27 victory after a late fumble recovery.

Live Live: Updates from every NFL Week 3 game

The 2-0 Bengals entered Acrisure Stadium as 3.5-point favorites over the Steelers, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but left Pittsburgh on Sunday with a disappointing loss.

The Steelers improved to 2-1 with a divisional win over the previously undefeated Bengals, led by three touchdown passes from its veteran quarterback.

In Rodgers' 22nd year, he opened the game with a 38-yard connection to Roman Wilson. Burrow and the Bengals answered with a short reception from Ja'Marr Chase before Rodgers notched his second touchdown pass of the first quarter, finding Ben Skowronek to give the Steelers a 14-7 lead.

Both teams settled in defensively in the second, with Cincinnati's Jordan Battle intercepting Rodgers to set up a five-play drive that ended with the Bengals finding the end zone on an impressive catch from Tee Higgins.

Cincinnati and Pittsburgh entered the half knotted at 17.

After eating up the clock with a 6:38 drive, the Bengals were held to a field goal in the third. Rodgers and the Steelers took the lead heading into the final quarter on a DK Metcalf touchdown, giving them a four-point advantage.

Mike Gesicki grabbed a wide open, 25-yard pass from Burrow to reclaim the lead early in the fourth, but a muffed punt by the Bengals set up the Steelers for a field goal to tie the game at 27 with 8:45 remaining.

A Steelers field goal gave them the lead with 2:15 left and put the ball in Burrow's hands for a two-minute drill.

Just after Burrow and Chase got the Bengals into field goal position with a chance to at least tie the game, Burrow was sacked on the very next play and fumbled the ball away, with Pittsburgh recovering to seal the upset win.

The Bengals will host the Jacksonville Jaguars next Sunday, while the Steelers hit the road to face the Cleveland Browns in a Thursday night game.

articles.title: Browns Beat Panthers, Box Score, Highlights for Deshaun Watson, Shedeur, Bryce Young, Top Players
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson's fourth-quarter heroics handed the Cleveland Browns their second straight win.
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson's fourth-quarter heroics handed the Cleveland Browns their second straight win.

Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for the game-winning touchdown with 1:48 left in the fourth to beat the Carolina Panthers 21-18 in Cleveland's home opener.

Watson hit Fannin in the end zone for the game-winning score that put the Browns over .500.

Fannin was Cleveland's top pass-catcher with seven receptions, 51 yards and a pair of touchdowns. The first of the two scores came in the first quarter to give the Browns a 10-point advantage.

Cleveland's lead lasted until the start of the fourth quarter. Carolina's fourth field goal of the contest handed the NFC South side a 12-10 lead.

Cleveland took the lead back on an Andre Szmyt field goal, but then Carolina rebounded again.

Bryce Young's only touchdown pass of the game was to John Metchie III with 4:25 left in the game.

Cleveland responded right away with Fannin's second touchdown catch of the day.

The Panthers had two more chances to get back in the lead, or at least tie, late in the fourth quarter, but the Browns came up with two straight stops.

The win gave the Browns their first winning record since the 2023 season.

The Browns are now tied with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals atop the AFC North at 2-1. The Browns play the Steelers on Thursday night. Carolina dropped to 1-2 and will try to rebound in Week 4 at home against the Detroit Lions.

articles.title: Steelers' defense comes up big against Joe Burrow, forces game-winning fumble in final minute
articles.summary: The Bengals and Steelers played a back-and-forth game in Week 3.
articles.body:
For 59 minutes, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow looked to be in control against a tough Pittsburgh Steelers defense. So when he got the ball back with a little over two minutes left to play, Steelers fans knew someone would have to come up big to seal the win.

Steelers defensive tackle Derrick Harmon got it done. Harmon sacked and stripped Burrow with just under a minute left to go and the Steelers leading by three. Pittsburgh recovered the ball with 44 seconds left and took a knee to win the contest 30-27.

It was one of the few mistakes made by Burrow the entire game. Prior to that fumble, Burrow had been the reason Cincinnati was in the game, taking what the Steelers gave him and coming up big when he took shots downfield.

Joe Burrow mostly impressive in Pittsburgh

Over his career, Burrow has excelled on the road against the Steelers. Sunday was no exception … until the final minute. Early on, Burrow was happy to take what the Steelers gave him, which was short completions. Burrow started the contest 14-of-14 for 95 yards and a touchdown. His first incomplete pass didn't come until the middle of the team's third drive.

While he played a safe game early, Burrow eventually needed to take a few shots against the Steelers. One of his first deep balls of the game came at the end of the first half, when Tee Higgins boxed out a defender to make a fantastic catch in the end zone for a score.

With the Bengals trailing by four in the fourth quarter, Burrow struck again, hitting tight end Mike Gesicki on a deep ball on fourth-and-2. The Steelers, expecting a run, allowed Gesicki to run by every defender and get wide open for the 25-yard touchdown.

That throw put Cincinnati up 27-24 at the start of the fourth quarter.

Burrow finished the contest 28-of-37, with 282 passing yards and three touchdowns. He took just one sack, the one that led to the game-losing fumble in the final minute.

Prior to the contest, Burrow held a 3-1 record at Pittsburgh. He had thrown nine touchdowns against four interceptions in those four games. While his touchdown and interception figures improved Sunday, he walked out of Pittsburgh with the loss.

Bengals' muffed punt lets Steelers back in game

Cincinnati's defense finally found some life on the next drive, stopping the Steelers and forcing a punt. But the Bengals' stop was all for nothing, as Ke'Shawn Williams fumbled the punt. Steelers wideout Ben Skowronek was there for the recovery, setting up Pittsburgh in prime condition for another score.

While the Steelers weren't able to get into the end zone on the drive, the team did kick a game-tying field goal with 8:47 to play.

The Steelers were then able to stop the Bengals' offense on the next drive, forcing a punt. Pittsburgh again failed to score a touchdown, but did add another field goal to take back the lead and go up 30-27.

Aaron Rodgers flashes his old form early vs. Bengals

Aaron Rodgers mostly matched Burrow, at least early in the contest. The 42-year-old Rodgers stirred the echoes of years past, picking apart the previously strong Bengals defense in the middle of the field early and often. The team's first three drives ended in scores, with Rodgers throwing two early touchdown passes and Chris Boswell hitting a field goal.

While Rodgers' next drive ended in an interception, it wasn't his fault. Rodgers was in line for another strong gain in the middle of the field, but his pass hit Roman Wilson right in the hands and bounced straight into Jordan Battle 's arms for the pick.

After Rodgers couldn't pull off a Hail Mary before halftime, he bounced back on the team's first drive of the third quarter, tossing another touchdown to give the Steelers the lead.

Rodgers found himself more limited later in the contest, with the Steelers forced to settle for field goals in the fourth quarter. That strategy nearly ended in disaster, as Burrow had plenty of time to lead a game-winning — or game-tying — drive at the end of the game before Pittsburgh's defense came up big.

Rodgers finished 19-of-34, with 292 yards, 3 touchdowns and an interception.

Following the contest, both teams sit at 2-1 in what looks to be a much-improved AFC North. The Bengals won't be allowed to rest in Week 4, as the team will take on the Jacksonville Jaguars (2-1) in Cincinnati.

The Steelers, meanwhile, will take on another division opponent, this time traveling to Ohio to take on the Cleveland Browns (2-1).

articles.title: Marcus Mariota leads Commanders past Sam Darnold, Seahawks in first start after Jayden Daniels' injury
articles.summary: Marcus Mariota got the start on Sunday after Jayden Daniels' gruesome elbow injury last week in Dallas.
articles.body:
Marcus Mariota had no problem filling in for Jayden Daniels .

Mariota led the Washington Commanders to a huge 33-31 upset win over Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks at Northwest Stadium on Sunday afternoon. The win marked the team's first of the season, and stopped what would have been its worst start to a campaign since 2019. It was also Mariota's first start since taking over for Daniels, who went down last week with a gruesome elbow injury.

The win was made possible only after Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold threw a rough interception to Kain Medrano right at midfield as Seattle was trying to mount a game-winning drive. Medrano then ran it back untouched to put the Commanders up by two scores for a second time in the second half.

Mariota looked solid for Washington on Sunday. He went 19 of 31 for 183 yards and threw three touchdowns early to give the Commanders a two-score lead in the third quarter. Mariota found Rachaad White for a 6-yard score in the first quarter, and then he hit Treylon Burks for an 11-yard touchdown in the second.

His best touchdown pass came early in the third quarter. Mariota, after scrambling out of the pocket, expertly found Terry McLaurin for a 30-yard score. That put Washington up 24-10 at the time.

Darnold and the Seahawks rallied and tied the game early in the fourth quarter after an 11-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba . It marked his second of the day, after his 1-yard score in the second quarter, and sixth of the season.

But after a late field goal and the pick 6, the Seahawks comeback started too late. A final touchdown, a Cooper Kupp score on a drive that took just 66 seconds, brought the Seahawks back within two. But Mariota and the Commanders held on to seal the two-point win. Mariota scrambled for 9 yards on a deep third down on the final drive to keep the clock moving.

Darnold went 31 of 45 for 379 yards with four touchdowns and two interceptions in the loss for Seattle. He made it back onto the field this week after missing last week's victory over the Arizona Cardinals due to a glute injury he suffered in Seattle's season-opener. Smith-Njigba had 128 yards and two touchdowns on 10 catches. The loss was the first of the season for the Seahawks.

McLaurin had 77 yards on six catches for the Commanders, and Stefon Diggs had another 33 yards on four catches. Jacory Croskey-Merritt led Washington on the ground with 36 yards on 19 carries.

Daniels went down with a dislocated elbow in a loss to the Dallas Cowboys last week. He is expected back in three weeks or sooner, according to the NFL Networks' Ian Rapoport, and he'll play with a brace on his elbow when he returns. The injury is similar to the one Daniels suffered last season . He missed four weeks with a dislocated elbow last year and re-injured himself in his first game back .

While it almost certainly won't be Mariota's team for long, he seems more than capable of holding things down for the Commanders for the time being. That's about all they can ask for.

There were no late-game boos in Cleveland on Sunday.

Deshaun Watson overcame early struggles against the Carolina Panthers to lead the Browns to a come-from-behind 21-18 win . The Browns QB led an eight-play, 65-yard drive in the game's final 4:19 that he capped with a touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr. to give the Browns a 19-18 lead.

He then found Denzel Boston in the end zone for a successful 2-point conversion.

The Panthers had two chances in the final two minutes at a drive to tie or take the lead. But the Browns' defense got the job done to ensure victory in Cleveland's home opener.

Cleveland and Carolina struggled to move the ball for most of the game

Most of Sunday's game was a slog for both offenses. The Browns carried a 10-9 lead into the fourth quarter as neither team found success moving the ball.

Panthers QB Bryce Young led a 72-yard drive that he capped with Carolina's first touchdown of the day on a pass to John Metchie to give the Panthers an 18-13 lead with 4:25 remaining.

That set Watson up with a chance to play the hero for the Browns, and he delivered with the 2:37 touchdown drive that featured a 21-yard scramble on third down in addition to his scoring pass. This also drew cheers from the Cleveland crowd.

When it was over, Watson celebrated the moment with fans cheering in the stands as he ran off the field.

Have Browns fans turned the corner on Watson?

When it was done, Watson had completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards with 2 touchdowns and no turnovers. He did most of his damage in the fourth quarter after tallying 67 yards on 3.2 yards per attempt through three.

His final line that added up to 4.8 yards per attempt was far from a thing a beauty. But it was enough to secure a win. And for Browns fans, that appears to have been enough for Watson to get back into their good graces. For now, at least.

A fan base that's weary of losing and was infuriated in the preseason by Watson earning the starting job appears to have now embraced its embattled quarterback amid a 2-1 start.

Watson's reception pregame, during early struggles

Much was made of Watson's anticipated reception for Cleveland's home opener after he helped the Browns to a Week 2 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, ensuring that he would remain Cleveland's starter in Week 3.

Watson had previously reached pariah status in the city due to a combination of years of poor play while on a $230 million contract and the two dozen women who accused him of sexual misconduct .

He was booed loudly at home in the preseason, then chastised Browns fans for voicing those feelings before head coach Todd Monken named him as starter over Shedeur Sanders .

Watson then played poorly on the road in a 34-10 Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , setting him up to potentially be benched with further poor play. But he played well enough to lead the Week 2 win over Tampa Bay and keep his job.

And Browns fans were largely subdued during pregame introductions as Watson and Sanders took the field together.

Scattered boos could be heard on the broadcast as Cleveland's offense struggled through the first three quarters Sunday, especially in the third quarter when Cleveland went three-and-out on three consecutive possessions.

But Browns fans were ultimately looking for a reason to cheer on Sunday, and despite Watson's history on and off the field, they ended Sunday's game by embracing his and the Browns' performance.

After the game, Monken spoke glowingly about Watson's late-game recovery and told reporters that he's 'happy for him." He stopped a reporter's question to make sure he got in his praise of his quarterback.

"We had not coached well enough on offense, we had not played well enough," Monken said. "He probably didn't play as well as he wanted. "But to get knocked down, come back in an make a play and then the 2-point conversion — this is about him. … I'm really happy for him."

"We had not coached well enough on offense, we had not played well enough," Monken said. "He probably didn't play as well as he wanted.

"But to get knocked down, come back in an make a play and then the 2-point conversion — this is about him. … I'm really happy for him."

Neither Watson nor Cleveland's offense have been lights-out through three weeks. But they've been good enough for a 2-1 start and to subdue any calls to give Sanders another shot as the starter after he struggled mightily last season as a rookie.

Next week will be another significant test for Watson as the Browns host a rejuvenated Steelers team that secured a 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday. As long as Cleveland keeps winning, Browns fans appear ready to embrace Watson as their quarterback.

articles.title: 49ers rule WR Mike Evans out vs. Cardinals with rib injury; Trent Williams leaves game on a cart
articles.summary: Evans joins an injured 49ers receiver corps that already features Ricky Pearsall and De'Zhaun Stribling.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers lost two more key players to injury against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.

Mike Evans left the game in the first half with a rib injury and was eventually ruled out. All-Pro left tackle Trent Williams then left in the third quarter on a cart with with a stinger. The 49ers initially listed Williams as questionable , and further details of his injury were unclear.

Evans ruled out; long-term status unclear

Evans was in clear pain and clutching his right side after running a route in the second quarter. He wasn't hit on the play, but needed the attention of medical trainers as he walked to the sideline.

Trainers then helped him as he walked gingerly on the sideline, and he eventually took to one knee, in obvious pain.

On the play before, Evans took a helmet to his left sight on a tackle by Budda Baker . It's not clear if that hit was related to Evans' injury.

Evans rode to the locker room on the back of a cart late in the first half and was ruled out before the start of the third quarter .

The 49ers didn't provide the precise nature of Evans' injury. He reportedly has a rib strain and will be evaluated further on Monday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Another injury blow to 49ers passing game

The injuries are unwelcome for a 49ers team that's been beset by injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Starter Ricky Pearsall is out for the season after undergoing preseason surgery to repair a damaged PCL. Standout rookie De'Zhaun Stribling is expected to miss roughly 10 weeks with an ankle injury sustained in San Francisco 's Week 1 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia.

Demarcus Robinson is on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain sustained in Week 2's win over the Miami Dolphins . Christian Kirk has been on injured reserve since the preseason with a lingering calf injury.

Evans joined the 49ers in the offseason after 12 standout seasons with Tampa Bay and immediately slotted in as their No. 1 option. With Evans sidelined alongside Pearsall and Stribling, the 49ers will rely even more in the passing on Deebo Samuel Sr., tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey in addition to backups Kaelon Black, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing .

Jefferson is hoping to stay healthy this season as he looks to bounce back from a relatively down year in 2025.

The star wide receiver finished the season having recorded 1,048 receiving yards on a career-low 12.5 yards per catch.

Jefferson is just two years removed from a stellar 2024 season during which he recorded 1,533 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns to help Sam Darnold and the Vikings compete for the top spot in the NFC.

Both Jefferson and his team, however, seemingly took a step back as rookie quarterback J.J. McCarthy struggled with injury and inconsistency in 2025.

Minnesota will hope to get Jefferson healthy in order to help the team improve after naming Kyler Murray starter earlier this offseason.

Murray's chemistry with Jefferson will be key to the Vikings' hopes of deploying a more effective offense this fall.

articles.title: NFL Week 3 Winners and Losers: What has happened to Drake Maye and the Patriots? 'My concern level is very high for this football team'
articles.summary: The Patriots are 1-2 and their quarterback has been a part of the problem.
articles.body:
It has been a long, long time since we've seen Drake Maye play well. It's hard to believe a 24-year-old quarterback who nearly won MVP in his second season could be so bad the following season that critics are having concerns about whether he still ranks as a top-10 quarterback, or maybe even top half of the league. But here we are.

After yet another bad game from the New England Patriots ' quarterback to extend a slump that dates back to last postseason, it's time to start wondering what's going on with Maye and how it's fixable.

He's missing throws. He is making mistakes that he rarely made last season. He's playing like a quarterback whose confidence is plummeting.

The Patriots were poor again on offense in a startling 35-6 road loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , who have a good but not stellar defense. Afterward, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel went so far as to say, "My concern level is very high for this football team."

At halftime, Maye had 88 passing yards and the Patriots had three points, which isn't nearly good enough. Maye made a huge mistake late in the first half that any NFL quarterback can't make, and epitomized the slump he has been in. On third-and-goal, Maye rolled out and was under some pressure. He threw back to the middle of the end zone, where he had nobody open. The blind pass looked like it was intended for Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter, who had an easy catch . Hunter made his first career interception and the Patriots' offensive issues continued.

If that was an isolated mistake from Maye, it might be a little easier to live with. But he had two awful interceptions against the Seahawks in the opener, including one into the end zone when the Patriots were in position to at least tie the game with a field goal. Maye didn't play great against the Steelers in Week 2 either, with no touchdowns and an interception. Then he struggled again against the Jaguars.

In the third quarter, trailing 14-3, Maye missed a third-down throw to Romeo Doubs , the Patriots missed a field goal and the Jaguars took the next possession in for a touchdown. At 21-3, it was practically over. A wayward pass that was easily picked off by Jaguars cornerback Jarrian Jones on New England 's next drive set up another Jacksonville touchdown and provided more misery for Maye. After that, CBS cameras found Vrabel with his arms on Maye's shoulders, giving him a pep talk. He needed it.

The excuses for Maye's bad stretch are valid. He has faced a brutal stretch of defenses, though those on the other side of the debate will point out how easy the Patriots' schedule was last season when he had a great season. Losing wideout A.J. Brown in the first game of the season to a high ankle sprain is a clear setback. The Patriots don't have many offensive playmakers to make up for his absence. But great quarterbacks are supposed to play well against great defenses and make up for the loss of star teammates, and Maye isn't doing that.

Maye was fine up until the end of last regular season. Then his passer rating dropped from a league-leading 113.5 in the regular season to 82.2 in the playoffs. That included a very quiet game in a Super Bowl blowout loss. This season, he has just one touchdown and led the NFL with four interceptions entering Week 3. Sunday against the Jaguars wasn't an easy assignment, but Maye shouldn't have struggled as he did. Maye was mercifully pulled from the blowout with a little more than eight minutes left, leaving Tommy DeVito to finish up. Maye finished 14 of 25 for 198 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions.

The Patriots should have been incredibly excited about their future after last season, even with the bad loss in the Super Bowl. They won the AFC and their quarterback was an instant star. And Maye should still be very good. But there are way more questions about that than anyone would have figured, just seven months after he came one vote from winning MVP.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 3 of the NFL season:

Jahmyr Gibbs : He is one of the best talents in the NFL, and on Sunday he had a touchdown run that would have made Marcus Allen proud. Or Barry Sanders.

The Detroit Lions running back took a toss to the right, was immediately hemmed in, so he reversed field and outran the New York Jets for a 17-yard score. It's the type of run that not many backs in the history of the league could even attempt, much less make it look as pretty as Gibbs did.

When the Jets came back to tie the game 24-24, Gibbs punched back. His 11-yard touchdown gave the Lions the lead again, and they went on to win, 31-24.

Gibbs had 99 yards rushing with two touchdowns, and 65 yards receiving and another score on seven catches.

Gibbs has gone from sharing time with David Montgomery to having the Lions' backfield to himself, and we're seeing him become an even bigger star.

Gibbs was fantastic again against the Jets. He signed a three-year, $67.5 million extension before this season began. It might be the biggest bargain in the NFL.

Aaron Rodgers : The veteran QB is continuing to do things at age 42 that only Tom Brady has done in the NFL.

Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers ' offense were shaky through two weeks, but in Week 3 they got a big divisional win over the Cincinnati Bengals . Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns, and the defense forced a fumble on a sack of Joe Burrow in the final minute to clinch a 30-27 win. Jaylen Warren also starred, with 127 rushing yards and 49 more receiving.

On the game-winning drive, two big pass plays from Rodgers set up a go-ahead field goal. He hit DK Metcalf for a 14-yard gain on first-and-11 after a holding penalty on Metcalf brought back a long run by Warren. Then Rodgers hit massive tight end Darnell Washington for 47 yards on a long run after catch, which got the Steelers into field-goal range. Rodgers played well in the second half despite getting banged up right before the end of the first half, when he went down on a passing attempt and Bengals defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence II hit him as he was moving. Rodgers gingerly walked off the field, but stayed in to help the Steelers get the win.

Rodgers has said this will be his final NFL season. If it is, he had at least one more vintage game in him. With maybe more to come.

Daniel Jones : The QB hasn't been great in his return from a torn Achilles. But when the Indianapolis Colts needed him Sunday, he came through.

The Houston Texans took a late 17-16 lead, and Jones had to move the Colts against a very tough defense. Jones hit Laquon Treadwell for 20 yards and Keenan Allen for 5 more, which was enough for Spencer Shrader to hit a 53-yard field goal for a 19-17 win. It was a rough loss for the Texans, who fell to 0-3, and a big one for the Colts. They started 0-2, including an overtime loss to the Chiefs last week that could have lingered. Blowing a lead to the Texans at home might have been devastating. But Jones had just enough to get Indianapolis over the finish line.

Marcus Mariota : The backup Commanders QB didn't have an easy assignment in his first start this season, replacing an injured Jayden Daniels . He had to face a Seattle Seahawks defense that won a Super Bowl last season and had allowed 17 points in two games this season.

Mariota and Washington put up 33 points on Seattle. Mariota threw three touchdowns and his 9-yard run with less than two minutes left sealed a 33-31 win.

Mariota gave it his all; he needed to get an IV in the fourth quarter.

"My workload hasn't been like this in a while," Mariota said, via Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic .

Mariota never took off to be a superstar, which was the hope for the Heisman Trophy winner when the Tennessee Titans made him the second pick of the 2015 NFL Draft. But he has settled in to be one of the best backup QBs in the NFL. The Commanders can count on him, as he showed against perhaps the NFL's best defense Sunday.

Cam Ward and the Titans: The weather was bad in New Jersey on Sunday. Still, the Tennessee Titans' offense shouldn't be this bad.

It was one step forward and two more back for the Titans. They played well against the Eagles in Week 2, though QB Cam Ward wasn't prolific and Philadelphia won in the final seconds. On Sunday, against a Giants team that was without Jaxson Dart and allowed 481 yards to the Rams last week, the Titans' offense was poor. But Tennessee still had a chance — when Ward made a horrible mistake.

On first-and-goal, trailing 12-7 in the final seconds, Ward was moving to his left. He had room to run and two timeouts. Instead, he threw to the end zone, right to safety Jevon Holland for a loss-clinching interception.

It was a terrible play from Ward. The Giants won 12-7 without scoring a touchdown.

It's three games into a new regime working with Ward and the results are the same as last season, when Ward struggled as a rookie. He threw for 140 yards in the opener and, although he played better last week against a good defense, it was just 183 yards. Ward had just 181 yards in Week 3 and made the mistake that ultimately ended his team's chance to win.

It has not been a good start for Ward in Year 2.

Jeff Hafley: Hafley, who is in his first NFL head coaching job, might already be wondering how long it'll take for him to get his first win.

On Sunday, the Dolphins played hard. QB Malik Willis was reasonable. The defense battled against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. And still, the Dolphins didn't really get close to a win. The Dolphins lost 24-10, falling to 0-3. The Chiefs put together a drive in the latter half of the fourth quarter to put away the game. Travis Kelce 's touchdown catch gave the Chiefs a 14-point lead with 2:55 to play.

The Dolphins lost their first game by 14 and their second game by 22. In a game they played reasonably well against Kansas City, they lost by 14. They also lost running back De'Von Achane , their best player, to a knee injury. The roster is incredibly thin on both sides of the ball. Miami 's schedule isn't easy. It's not going to be a fun season in Miami.

The Chargers are a sloppy team, and even though the Bills were giving the ball away, the Chargers couldn't take advantage in a 24-16 loss. A missed field goal by Cameron Dicker in the first half cost Los Angeles momentum when they were up 10-0. Justin Herbert threw a bad interception in the fourth quarter. A bad drop by Quentin Johnston on third-and-10 was costly. Ultimately, Josh Allen did enough to get his team the win, even though he and the Bills weren't at their best.

The Chargers needed a win. Their 0-2 start against the Cardinals and Raiders put them in a huge hole, with a tough schedule coming up. They had a double-digit lead and the defense was making big plays. And it still wasn't enough to win.

Panthers defense: This unit was a problem in a Week 1 loss, allowing 59 points. It couldn't close the door on Sunday either.

Carolina's offense didn't do much against the Cleveland Browns , but the Panthers scored in the fourth quarter to provide an 18-13 lead. All the Panthers had to do was keep Deshaun Watson and the Browns out of the end zone. Watson hadn't done much to that point. But the beleaguered quarterback had a highlight for the second straight week, driving the Browns 65 yards and hitting Harold Fannin Jr. for the tight end's second touchdown of the game to give the Browns a 21-18 lead.

Watson was helped when his interception was wiped off the board due to a questionable roughing the passer penalty on linebacker Bobby Okereke , but Carolina had other chances and couldn't get a stop. The Panthers couldn't answer on offense and Cleveland had the win. They're 2-1.

The Panthers won the NFC South last season but are 1-2 to start this season. The defense was without linebacker Devin Lloyd on Sunday, but it will still look at the late loss as a missed opportunity.

articles.title: Vikings WR Justin Jefferson leaves game vs. Buccaneers early with ankle injury
articles.summary: Justin Jefferson had two catches on the Vikings' opening drive on Sunday afternoon.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings lost star wide receiver Justin Jefferson after their opening drive on Sunday afternoon in Florida.

Jefferson went down with an ankle injury early in their matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers despite him appearing to get off to a very normal start at Raymond James Stadium. He caught a deep 22-yard pass from Kyler Murray on the Vikings ' first play of the game, and later caught a 10-yard screen pass to set up an early 54-yard field goal from Will Reichard .

But that was it for Jefferson. He didn't make it back onto the field on the next Vikings drive, and instead went into the blue medical tent on the sideline for quite some time. The Vikings quickly said that he was dealing with an ankle injury, and was questionable to return.

A closer look revealed Jefferson's left ankle awkwardly being rolled up on as he was tackled on that second reception.

Specifics of the injury are not yet known.

Jefferson was spotted back on the Vikings' sideline later in the first half walking around, but he didn't enter the game again. He later walked to the locker room.

Eventually, the Vikings ruled him out for good early in the third quarter.

Jefferson entered Sunday with 147 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns so far this season, his seventh in the league. The 26-year-old had 1,048 yards last season, which was actually a career low, despite it being his sixth straight campaign with at least 1,000 receiving yards.

The Vikings are a perfect 2-0 so far this season. They rallied past the Green Bay Packers in their season-opener and then beat the Chicago Bears in a sloppy, rainy 9-3 battle last week at Soldier Field.

This post will be updated with more information shortly.
