Marcus Mariota threw three touchdown passes as the Washington Commanders claimed a 33-31 victory over Seattle to end the Seahawks' long winning streak.

Seattle had won a dozen games in a row, following up last season's Super Bowl triumph by starting their campaign with back-to-back triumphs, but Mariota starred in the absence of the injured Jayden Daniels .

Also crucial in the Commanders' first win of the season was Kain Medrano intercepting Sam Darnold 's pass and sprinting 50 yards for a touchdown as Seattle tasted defeat for the first time since November.

Chris Boswell kicked the go-ahead field goal as the Pittsburgh Steelers bounced back from their defeat to the New England Patriots by edging out the Cincinnati Bengals 30-27.

The Bengals' hopes of avoiding a first defeat of the season ended when Joe Burrow fumbled in the final minute after being strip-sacked by Derrick Harmon .

Trevor Lawrence threw touchdown passes for Josh Cameron, Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington to lift the Jacksonville Jaguars to an impressive 35-6 win over the Patriots.

Injuries continue to mount up for the New York Giants, who lost quarterback Jaxson Dart last week and Brian Burns went off with a knee problem in a 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans .

Spencer Shrader 's 53-yard field goal, his fourth of the game, helped the Indianapolis Colts defeat the Houston Texans 19-17.

Deshaun Watson and Harold Fannin Jr combined for two touchdown passes as the Cleveland Browns overcame the Carolina Panthers 21-18.

Josh Allen 's two rushing touchdowns led the Buffalo Bills to a 24-16 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Miami Dolphins 24-10 and the Detroit Lions beat the New York Jets 31-24.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Bills' NFL Week 3 Game vs. Chargers
articles.summary: It wasn't pretty, but the Buffalo Bills are 3-0.
articles.body:
It wasn't pretty, but the Buffalo Bills are 3-0.

The mistake-prone Bills recovered from a horrible start to beat the Los Angeles Chargers 24-16 at Highmark Stadium on Sunday. It was a roller-coaster ride of an affair, but a W nonetheless.

Here are my grades for all of the key players from Sunday's victory.

It was not a crisp performance from Allen, who looked a little out of sorts and made some questionable decisions. He threw two first-half interceptions and fumbled in the third quarter, completing just 16 passes in an up-and-down performance.

Allen eventually played the superhero role and continued to build his MVP resume while leading the Bills to 14 points in the fourth quarter. But the mistakes above combined with an uncharacteristic unwillingness to take several great rushing opportunities result in a B grade here.

That's back-to-back superb showings from Cook, who fumbled on the first play from scrimmage but compensated for that the rest of the day with critical run after critical run.

He finished with 154 yards and a touchdown, with 39 of those yards coming on his last five carries.

Johnson had an absolutely sick catch-and-run touchdown negated by a penalty, but he still caught four passes on four targets for 50 yards on just 15 snaps.

Clearly far from 100 percent healthy, the veteran receiver battled and made some key catches. He finished with six grabs for 67 yards on 10 targets in an admirable performance. Three of those came on third down.

It was a quiet afternoon from Shakir, who caught just a single six-yard pass on three targets. But that one reception did move the chains on a third down in the fourth quarter.

Just one catch here as well, but Coleman made a great adjustment on a 37-yard gain to reach the 1-yard line, setting up a momentum-shifting touchdown drive late in the first half. He also had an onside kick recovery to ice the game.

Just 21 snaps for Palmer, who was targeted zero times and was generally a ghost.

Week 3 Waiver Wire Targets to Replace Fantasy Players on Injury List

Back to earth for the standout from the first two weeks of the season. Two receptions for 38 yards and an unforgivable fumble in which he was extremely careless with the ball.

Just a single five-yard catch in a fairly quiet game for Knox, but he did make some nice blocks in pass protection.

His holding penalty wiped out a highlight-reel touchdown by Johnson, and while he was held catchless, he remained stout as a run blocker.

The vet took a pair of penalties and was responsible for a sack as well as multiple hurries on Allen.

Two holding penalties for the first-year starter, one of which wiped out a big Cook run that led to an Allen interception on the very next play.

He helped set up some of Cook's best runs but also gave up a sack to kill a first-quarter drive.

Torrence was responsible for more pressure than you'd like, but he and the right side of the line did a tremendous job opening up holes for the run game.

See Torrence. Brown was also beaten in a few critical spots but executed superbly as a run blocker. He sprang Cook with a killer block on a game-icing first-down run late in the fourth quarter.

The highly paid veteran led the way on a key fourth-quarter pressure that resulted in a Los Angeles turnover on downs, but he was again held without a sack and he took a silly unnecessary roughness penalty.

That's three consecutive two-sack performances from Rousseau, who was also stellar in run defense. He's a legit Defensive Player of the Month candidate.

The sophomore was on a heater before "cooling off" with "only" five quarterback pressures against a weak offensive line on Sunday.

He made some stops and brought a little bit of pressure but there were no standout plays for a guy who was limited to 28 snaps in his return from a hip injury.

I actually really liked what I saw from Jackson in all facets over a 26-snap showing. He got awesome penetration to deflect a Justin Herbert pass in a big spot as the Bills were attempting to stay within reaching distance late in the first half.

For the second week in a row, the former third-round pick was steady across the board as part of the rotation up front.

He looked lost on a couple of occasions in the first half and is still generally not in on enough of the action. Far too often, Bernard is nowhere to be found.

Williams led the team with nine tackles in what was easily his best game of the season so far. He had two great tackles in goal-to-go situations.

It was harder to judge the corners Sunday as the Bills spent a lot more time in zone, but Benford again struggled overall when it came to coverage and tackling before suffering an injury late in the third quarter. He also took a holding penalty that canceled out a C.J. Gardner-Johnson interception.

Very limited damage and no major mistakes from the sophomore first-rounder. The Bills might want to see if he is the better option as the No. 1 corner.

The rookie second-round pick relieved Benford and immediately forced a third-and-long with perfect coverage on the boundary. He also contributed with a solid tackle on a scrambling Herbert in the fourth quarter. He and Hairston were later beaten on a big third down but were saved by a dropped pass from Quentin Johnston.

The Chargers got some life late in the game when Alford was beaten badly and then missed a tackle, leading to a big gain. He generally struggled in coverage and dropped a relatively easy interception but was pretty strong inside the box.

Beyond his massive interception and return in the fourth quarter, the 28-year-old newcomer shined in coverage. He made a clutch tackle on a third-and-goal play that forced the Chargers to kick a field goal, and he also had a pick negated by a penalty.

No big plays but also no major gaffes from the steady third-year starter.

He made his lone field-goal attempt and went 3-for-3 on extra points.

What a pickup this has turned into. Dortch brought the opening kickoff back to the 43-yard line and was fine beyond that in a mistake-free game.

articles.title: Saints RB Travis Etienne leaves game vs. Raiders early with apparent hamstring injury
articles.summary: Travis Etienne pulled up awkwardly and reached for his hamstring in the second half of their matchup with the Raiders on Sunday afternoon.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints lost running back Travis Etienne early on Sunday afternoon due to an apparent hamstring injury.

Etienne took a handoff in the second half of their matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday afternoon, and started breaking for the right sideline at the Caesars Superdome. Suddenly, though, Etienne reached back for his left hamstring and was clearly in some discomfort. He was hit out of bounds, but came up limping and left the field for the medical tent.

Eventually, Etienne made his way to the locker room. The Saints called him questionable to return with the hamstring injury, though further specifics are not yet known.

Etienne had a team-high 57 rushing yards on 13 carries when he left the game. He had another 13 receiving yards on two catches. The 27-year-old entered the contest with 71 rushing yards so far this season, his first with the Saints after spending his first four years in the league with the Jacksonville Jaguars . The Saints reached a four-year, $52 million deal with him in free agency this past offseason.

Despite losing Etienne, the Saints scored immediately after his 16 yard run in the third quarter. Quarterback Tyler Shough threw a 16-yard touchdown pass to Noah Fant on the next play, which put them up 27-16 at the time.

That marked Shough's fourth touchdown pass of the game. He found Fant for a 3-yard score earlier in the second quarter, and he hit fellow tight end Juwan Johnson for a pair of short touchdowns, too.

This post will be updated with more information shortly.

articles.title: ‘There’s Overreactions’: Aaron Rodgers Silences Talking Heads in Win over Bengals
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH — There were a slew of negative headlines throughout last week after the Pittsburgh Steelers’ ugly 20-3 loss to […]
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH — There were a slew of negative headlines throughout last week after the Pittsburgh Steelers ' ugly 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots . There was even a report that the Steelers were going through a Mike Tomlin hangover .

The Steelers certainly quieted the noise with their 30-27 upset over the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday.

It just shows any given Sunday. Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers pointed out in his postgame interview that there's a lot overreaction in today's media.

"Listen, I know the media day and age that we're in there's overreactions when we put up 3 points and look like dog you know what," Rodgers said. "We had a nice game today. We put up over 400 yards and 30 points, and it could have been a lot more. But every week is a different week, different challenge, different opponent, different defense."

Coming into Sunday's game, the Steelers accumulated 499 yards, which ranked 30th in the NFL, and the Tennessee Titans follow with just 486 yards, which is 31st in the NFL.

To put that in perspective, Steelers punter Cameron Johnston leads the NFL with 579 yards on 12 punts, which also leads the league, and Titans punter Tommy Townsend is third in the league with 529 yards on 11 punts.

The Steelers looked abysmal on offense to start the season, but they were hitting on all cylinders against Cincinnati.

Making changes on the offensive line paid off big .

Rookie right tackle Max Iheanachor and guard Brock Hoffman started on the right side on Sunday. They replaced — Dylan Cook and Spencer Anderson — who reportedly has a broken bone in his right leg — respectively.

Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes (55.9%) for 292 yards with three touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 101.6

Rodgers got ripped by Skip Bayless earlier this week. The prominent sports media figure said the four-time NFL MVP was washed .

" Aaron Rodgers is washed. I have to keep saying this, and I don't hear people in the media say it at all," Bayless said.

"He should've retired four years ago after his final year in Green Bay. For four years he's been done, and I've said it for four years. He's just completely over the hill. He's lost his poise and guts in the pocket; he won't stand in; he just tries to dink-and-dunk; he's a turnover machine."

That's a perfect example of an overreaction after just one bad game in Week 2 of the season.

Rodgers certainly silenced Bayless on Sunday.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Reacts to Browns Fans' Cheers in Win vs. Bryce Young, Panthers After Prior Comments
articles.summary: All it took was a pair of victories for Cleveland Browns veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson to win over his home fans.
articles.body:
All it took was a pair of victories for Cleveland Browns veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson to win over his home fans.

After leading the Browns to a 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday to improve to 2-1, Watson praised the fans at Huntington Bank Field for helping to fuel the victory.

"The energy, the fans, it was amazing," Watson told reporters. "They kept believing in us, kept the energy up. ... We didn't give up, we fed off that energy."

Of course, Watson's comments are a stark contrast to his disparaging reaction to hearing boos from Cleveland fans during the preseason.

Watson and the Browns incurred some boos after falling behind 18-13 in the fourth quarter, but he said he didn't notice as he spearheaded the comeback victory.

"I didn't hear any of that, but at the same time, I'm just trying to give them something to cheer about and get that W, so that was all that mattered," Watson told reporters.

Watson and the Browns will look to make it three straight wins when they meet the Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) on Thursday Night Football in Week 4.

articles.title: Fired Up Dan Campbell Hands Out 3 Game Balls Following Win vs. Jets
articles.summary: Fired-up Lions coach Dan Campbell handed game balls to Jahmyr Gibbs, Jacob Saylors and Chuck Clark after Detroit's 31-24 win over the Jets.
articles.body:
Dan Campbell had plenty to be fired up about following the Detroit Lions ' 31-24 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday at Ford Field.

It wasn't always pretty. Detroit watched a 24-10 fourth-quarter lead disappear before Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs connected for the go-ahead touchdown with 2:25 remaining. Then, with the Jets threatening to tie it again, Chuck Clark came screaming through on a safety blitz, sacked Geno Smith and forced a fumble that Jack Campbell recovered to end it.

Afterward, Campbell praised all three phases of his team.

And when it came time to hand out game balls, he had one for each.

The offensive game ball went to Gibbs, and this one required approximately zero debate.

Gibbs finished with 20 carries for 99 yards and two rushing touchdowns, then added seven receptions for 65 yards and another score. His 11-yard touchdown reception in the final minutes ultimately proved to be the game-winner.

His two rushing touchdowns also pushed him past Lions legend Billy Sims for second place on Detroit's all-time rushing touchdown list, trailing only Barry Sanders.

It was also another historic afternoon for Gibbs, who became the first player in NFL history to open a season with at least 300 rushing yards, four rushing touchdowns, 150 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns through three games.

Jacob Saylors Delivered on Special Teams

Campbell's special-teams game ball went to Jacob Saylors , whose contributions won't jump off the traditional offensive box score.

Saylors delivered two kickoff returns for 81 yards, giving Detroit excellent field position at its own 38 and 47-yard lines. In a game ultimately decided by one possession, those hidden yards were significant.

It's exactly the type of contribution Campbell has always valued. Detroit didn't dominate the Jets Sunday. It needed help from everywhere.

With Detroit leading 31-24 and New York already inside Lions territory during the final minute, Clark blitzed up the middle and got to Smith before the Jets quarterback could escape.

Clark's sack knocked the football loose. Jack Campbell recovered it, and Detroit's offense came onto the field to kneel out the victory.

It was an especially satisfying moment for a defense that entered Sunday looking for answers after allowing 41 points against Buffalo and had again surrendered a double-digit advantage against New York.

And after a 31-24 win that required contributions from all three, Campbell made sure each got its moment.
